page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256gb is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64 and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is network-attached with a local boot capacity of 1 GB, and there are no integrated GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory performance, achieving a top-tier rating in PassMark memory score and large-block write memory bandwidth of 196.72 GB/sec. Single-core CPU performance is highly competitive, with Geekbench single-core scores of 2588.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 40.57 GB/sec reaching top-tier levels. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 62580.25 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20519.0. The system also exhibits strong capabilities in database operations, handling 63.76 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 22635.98 in PassMark database tests.

The hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff: while memory bandwidth and single-core execution speeds are excellent, multi-core CPU performance and small-block cached memory reads remain in the average tier. The lack of substantial local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads. Qualitatively, the high memory density relative to the vCPU count makes this instance cost-efficient for memory-bound applications that do not require massive parallel compute scaling. It is well-suited for large-scale database hosting, in-memory caching, software compilation, text and image processing pipelines, and medium-scale language model inference.
